external_submission.title: Evidence, Policy, and Settlement in Energy-Linked Financial Claims
external_submission.author: Christopher Ongko
external_submission.affiliation: MS Program in Finance, College of Management, Yuan Ze University, Taoyuan, Taiwan

research_question: Once external evidence is available, how should a financial decision distinguish source assurance, policy admission, supported physical quantity before valuation, and later settlement?

prior_art_not_claimed_novel: oracle delivery of external data and oracle trust models
research_positioning.bounded_contribution: A reproducible fixed-evidence experiment that keeps source assurance, policy admission, supported physical quantity, and settlement as separate decision stages.
research_positioning.policy_status: research configurations used for sensitivity analysis; not calibrated, institutionally endorsed, or economically optimal
research_positioning.quantity_interpretation: 33.066 kWh is a derived physical surplus quantity used before valuation; it is not a monetary price, market value, or legal entitlement
research_positioning.surplus_derivation: per interval max(PV generation - general load - controlled load, 0); derived surplus, not directly metered export

references: Eskandari et al. 2021, SoK: Oracles from the Ground Truth to Market Manipulation
W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0, 2025
Dagher et al. 2015, Provisions: Privacy-preserving Proofs of Solvency for Bitcoin Exchanges
Ratnam et al. 2017, Residential load and rooftop PV generation: an Australian distribution network dataset
